title: Chapter 33 — Struthioniformes
description: Ostriches — the largest living birds. Struthioniformes includes the flightless ratites of Africa. Ostriches are the fastest birds on land, reaching speeds of 70 km/h, and lay the largest eggs of any living bird. Males are striking black-and-white; females are brown.

children.name: Struthio
children.description: The only extant genus in the family, comprising the largest living birds on Earth. Flightless and powerfully built, they are adapted for high-speed running across African savannas.

children.name: Struthio camelus
children.description: The common ostrich (Struthio camelus), or simply ostrich, is a species of flightless bird native to certain areas of Africa (and historically, Arabia) and is the largest living species of bird.

children.name: Struthio molybdophanes
children.description: The Somali ostrich (Struthio molybdophanes), also known as the blue-necked ostrich, is a large flightless bird native to the Horn of Africa.
